text.p: Italian BTP futures started on a firmer note but soon slipped back to largely steady levels in early trade before sellers moved in and pushed contracts prices lower after around 30 minutes of trading, dealers said.

The uncertain start came after two days of losses for BTP futures, while the market was awaiting a statement from the German cabinet today set to call for a strong mark. German finance minister Theo Waigel said the statement was due today.
"The market is a little unsettled by the weakness of the mark and is waiting to see how strong the German statement will be on the currency," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that after BTPs had risen so fast so quickly there was always likely to be profit taking at such high levels, while the strength of the dollar and weakness of the mark was causing concern for the future single European currency.

They added that the strong lira had given support to BTPs in the rally over the last month, but the weakness of the mark was now starting to raise some concerns in the wider context of the future of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union.
Official data showing Italian May industrial production rose an adjusted 0.3 percent month/month had little impact on the Italian BTP market, dealers said.

Dealers said that the BTP futures market was likely to continue under pressure for the rest of the day, and the LIFFE Sept futures contract had drifted off 12 basis points to 135.42 after around 45 minutes of trading.
